_due is not a predicate — it RECORDS the step and returns True. FROZEN = torch.randn(V, D) at module scope, unconditional, V == VMAX. Coverage: read all 8,342 lines of the file. No BLOCKED sources.

Shape of this chunk: it opens on a tokenizer-quality investigation and ends with the entire comparative program being invalidated. The arc worth carrying forward is that almost every quantitative claim made in the first two days was withdrawn by the third, and the withdrawals were mostly triggered by the researcher pushing back rather than by Claude's own checks.

Researcher's highest-leverage interventions, in order of impact:
1. "Why is vmax8 eliminated? I don't think we ran it properly, and that statement constrains us a lot" — forced a full retraction of a premature elimination and reopened the top-end probe.
2. "why would it work in the 4k, not either other? ... I suspect a bug may have occured" — non-monotonicity read as a bug, not a property. Correct: led directly to the FROZEN RNG discovery that invalidated the whole VMAX comparison.
3. "Why always the smoke tests? Are they even updated?" — the smoke had drifted from the grid within an hour, and Claude's first fix would have passed seven identical runs as seven arms.
4. "the final goal is for language, not optimizing specifically the tokenizer, vmax, or different ways to freeze the structure ... a target has been and still is the continual learning" — the session-level course correction; Claude conceded drift and that no checkpoint had been saved for anything.
5. The LR requirement "a replicate, and b improve" exposed a real bug (1.0 % 1.0 == 0.0 jumping the LR back to peak on the final steps of every 8-epoch run).

The single most important structural fact established: the repo's own code at ground_update documents a same-seed spread of 1.594 b/B ("two runs with byte-identical model code and the same seed ... read 3.694 and 2.100"). Nearly every comparison made in this chunk was of differences smaller than that, from n=1 runs. Claude's own closing summary: "this system cannot resolve anything below ~1.6 b/B from single runs."

What survives at chunk end (Claude's own list, and it looks right): the dead-row series (0% -> ~2.2 b/B vs 75% -> 6.1, consistent across many runs and far outside the spread); the base/nogate byte-identical determinism check (exact, not statistical); and the code-level bug findings, which are facts about the source rather than measurements.

Container instability is a recurring hazard, not a footnote: the checkout rolled back to commit 2c705c7 at least four times (23:26, 01:16, 02:39, 12:22, 01:42, 19:08, 21:31 across the chunk). Nothing was lost because everything was pushed to origin promptly, but one arm-audit agent read a stale checkout and returned a wrong finding as a result.

A note on Claude's error rate in this window: of the bugs found, roughly half were introduced by Claude during this same chunk (_hb collision, ragged-window ValueError, the entropy gate shipped twice broken, the gate default that starved a pilot, the _due retok double-call that killed re-segmentation for three 18-epoch runs, the _due('probation') KeyError, the incomplete VMAX-513 frozen fix, the failed first RNG fix). The pattern the researcher is implicitly pushing against — ship, default-on, then discover — recurs throughout.

Wrong statistic: the constructed test used repetitive text; on real English H is median 3.48 / p90 4.39 and is ANTI-correlated with frequency, so 1.5 bits rejects the most useful merges first. Wrong control flow: a rejected candidate returned None, aborting the grow burst. Replaced by p(b|a) with a filtering loop.
